items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024

ctx.x: Probably. But a friend who is a bass player and a contractor and he said, “Never confess.” A lot of times if you make a mistake it’s up to them to hear it. You don’t want to confess your mistakes because they might just be going to do another take anyway. And a lot of times they do. So it’s just one of those things.

I once asked Bucky Pizzarelli what kind of date might he have done that would be worth coming home and talking to his wife Ruth about — “Hey guess what occurred today.” Do you have one of those, like with all the work you do, what is worth bringing up when you get home?

Oh I always comment about what I just did. You know like I played a Dixieland gig Sunday night and I came home and told my wife, “That was like a lot of fun, like I really loved playing that bass. I got the sound that I wanted to get, you know, you don’t play with any microphone or amplifier and the place was sold out to a tour of Japanese tourists, older people. And they ended up like really getting into this, dancing and throwing up their hands and during the break they’d run up on the bandstand and pose
